forces.title: Large utilities divest non-core water operations
forces.description: Major power and utilities companies in Europe are increasingly divesting non-core assets, including water operations, to sharpen their portfolio focus on electric businesses. This trend, driven by a desire for simplification and to reduce capital allocation to diversified holdings, represents a significant structural shift for the water supply and treatment sector. While it poses a potential headwind for integrated multi-utilities, it also creates opportunities for pure-play water companies or private capital firms to acquire and specialize in water infrastructure, reshaping ownership and investment landscapes within IN100301.
forces.source_title: The New Rules of M&A in Power and Utilities

forces.title: Irish water quality regulations driving nutrient management
forces.description: Ireland's Nitrates Action Programme and ongoing water quality assessments are leading to stronger nutrient management measures and anticipated regulatory tightening. This development acts as a significant tailwind for the water supply and treatment sector, particularly in wastewater treatment and source water protection. It necessitates increased investment in advanced treatment technologies, infrastructure upgrades, and monitoring solutions to comply with evolving environmental policies, ensuring the long-term sustainability and quality of water resources for end-users.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Agriculture Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Population growth and climate change strain drinking water supply
forces.description: Across many regions in Europe, drinking water systems face increasing pressure from population growth and the escalating frequency of droughts due to climate change. This creates significant challenges for water collection, treatment, and distribution to end-users, highlighting a structural tailwind for the IN100301 sector. It will drive demand for enhanced water resource management strategies, investments in new water sources, advanced treatment technologies like desalination, and more resilient distribution infrastructure to ensure reliable supply.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: EU Water Framework Directive boosts Dutch sewerage investment
forces.description: The European Water Framework Directive is a key driver for increased maintenance and investment in the Dutch infrastructure sector, specifically leading to projects like sewerage improvement and flood defense reinforcement. This represents a direct tailwind for the Water Supply & Treatment sector (IN100301), particularly for wastewater treatment components and related infrastructure. Compliance with the directive, coupled with climate adaptation efforts, mandates continuous upgrades and expansion of facilities to manage water quality and quantity, ensuring robust utility services for end-users.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector
